title: Haben and Sein
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; some example sentences were reconstructed from context and may differ slightly from the video.
objectives: I can conjugate haben with all pronouns
I can conjugate sein with all pronouns
I can choose the right form for a noun or a name as the subject
I can build simple sentences with haben and sein

expressions.en: You have a girlfriend / female friend.

expressions.de: Frau Schmidt, sind Sie zu Hause?
expressions.en: Mrs Schmidt, are you at home?

grammar.title: Conjugation of haben (to have)
grammar.body: *Haben* and *sein* are the two most important verbs. They are used as main verbs and also as helping verbs (you will meet this later). The verb always agrees with the subject. *Haben* follows the regular endings, except that *du hast* and *er/sie/es hat* lose the *b*.

grammar.title: Conjugation of sein (to be)
grammar.body: *Sein* is a special verb: it does **not** follow the regular endings. You simply have to learn the forms by heart. Note that *wir* and *sie / Sie* use the same form: *sind*.
grammar.ar: الفعل sein شاذّ: يجب حفظ تصريفاته كما هي.

examples.de: Frau Schmidt, sind Sie zu Hause?
examples.en: Mrs Schmidt, are you at home?

grammar.title: Names and nouns as subject
grammar.body: When the subject is a name or a noun, think of the pronoun that could replace it and use that verb form. *Maria* can be replaced by *sie* (she), so: *Maria hat ...*, *Maria ist ...*. *Anna und Tom* could be replaced by *sie* (they), so: *Anna und Tom haben ...*, *Anna und Tom sind ...*.

examples.en: Maria has a house. (Maria = sie, singular)

examples.de: Anna und Tom haben ein Kind.
examples.en: Anna and Tom have a child. (= sie, plural)

mistakes.why: *Haben* loses the b: du hast, er hat.
In German age is expressed with *sein*.

pronunciation.tip: The *h* is breathed. *hat* sounds like 'hut' with a short a: *hat*, *hast*.
*s* at the start of a word is voiced, like English z: *sind*, *seid*.

lines.de: Hallo, Frau Schmidt! Sind Sie zu Hause?
lines.en: Hello, Mrs Schmidt! Are you at home?

lines.de: Ja, ich bin zu Hause. Wir haben heute Zeit.
lines.en: Yes, I am at home. We have time today.

lines.de: Ja, wir haben ein Kind. Es ist glücklich.
lines.en: Yes, we have a child. It is happy.

tip: Learn the pronouns and the verb forms together as a table. Cover one column and test yourself.

comprehension.q: What is the *du* form of haben?
What is the *ihr* form of sein?
Which form of sein is used for *wir* and *sie / Sie*?
Which pronoun can replace *Maria*, and which form of haben follows?
Which of the two verbs has no regular endings?

exercises.title: Conjugate haben
exercises.instructions: Write the correct form of haben.

exercises.title: Conjugate sein
exercises.instructions: Write the correct form of sein.

summary: haben: ich habe, du hast, er/sie/es hat, wir haben, ihr habt, sie/Sie haben.
sein: ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind.
Both verbs are used as main verbs and as helping verbs.
With a name or noun as subject, use the form of the pronoun that could replace it.
Age is expressed with sein: Ich bin 20 Jahre alt.
